name: Programming Language Concepts
summary: The ideas shared by all programming languages (syntax, binding, scope, evaluation, types, control and objects), learned partly by writing interpreters.

topics.name: Language design goals and programming paradigms
Syntax: grammars, BNF and abstract syntax trees
Names, bindings and scope (static versus dynamic)
Evaluation strategies: call-by-value, call-by-name and call-by-need
Type systems: static versus dynamic, strong versus weak, type inference
Polymorphism: parametric, subtype and ad hoc
Writing an interpreter for a small language
Memory management: stack, heap and garbage collection
Control abstractions: exceptions, continuations and coroutines
Object models: classes, prototypes, mixins and traits
